beats.head: Aldousspire Group to Extend Heirloom Format Abroad After Domestic Success
beats.body: Building on profitable concept stores, Mira Ashby announced plans to open the first fifteen Heirloom locations in overseas markets over the next 18 months. The rollout marks Aldousspire's largest international push in a generation, backed by a dedicated £90M fit-out budget. Ashby said the everyday line would anchor the new stores while heirloom pieces drive footfall.

beats.head: Boreas Power Signs Second Anchor Pact to Extend Campus Network Eastward
beats.body: Mira Thorne secured a $2.8B supply agreement to underwrite a second cluster of compute-paired campuses, days after energizing the first site. The deal names an unspecified consortium as anchor offtaker and covers power and storage capacity through the next decade. Thorne said groundbreaking on the eastern cluster would begin within two quarters.

beats.head: Carrowwell Edges Past Estimates as Second Machines Plant Reaches Full Output
beats.body: Mara Voss reported a narrow beat as the second machines plant hit full production, lifting group revenue 9% on the quarter. Automated material-handling orders continued to build, though Voss flagged softening in auto parts demand as a watch item. Guidance for the year was left unchanged.

beats.head: Holtware Co. Extends Modular Platform Into Outdoor and Garden Tools
beats.body: Aurelia Dray unveiled a dozen new cordless outdoor tools sharing the modular battery platform introduced last year, targeting the higher-margin seasonal segment. The lineup includes trimmers, blowers and a compact mower, all cross-compatible with existing packs. Dray said early retailer commitments already exceed the initial platform rollout's.

beats.head: Kesselgrove Co. to Add Third Bay as Press Backlog Hits Historic Low
beats.body: With its press backlog now at a record low, Orla Steg approved construction of a third assembly bay to capture demand that current capacity can no longer absorb quickly. The $180M project will lift annual press output by roughly a third when it reaches full production in two years. Steg framed the move as measured expansion rather than a departure from the company's disciplined pace.

beats.head: Korrwright Works Acquires Verenne Case-Maker Dovreux Frères in $620M Deal
beats.body: Dunmore Carrow announced the purchase of storied case and dial specialist Dovreux Frères, bringing another rung of the supply chain in-house just months after the Halbrook Perpetual's prize win. The all-cash deal absorbs Dovreux's three ateliers and roughly 480 finishers, and Carrow said its guilloché workshop would supply the entire Halbrook line by next season. Analysts noted it is Korrwright's largest single acquisition in over a decade.

beats.head: Marlgear Supply Ousts Corin Blakely as Board Names Turnaround Chief Amid Kessel Fallout
beats.body: The board removed Corin Blakely after the Kessel fault scandal, the $1.4B suit and the disruptive consumer exit eroded remaining investor confidence. Incoming chief Renna Halvorsen, a veteran of two industrial restructurings, will inherit the ongoing prosecution referral and a slimmed device line. Halvorsen pledged a full safety review and settlement talks as her first priorities.

beats.head: Stegforge Beats Again as Consortium Locks Multi-Year Rail Plate Offtake
beats.body: Aurelia Steg reported quarterly earnings above consensus, crediting a newly signed multi-year offtake agreement that reserves the bulk of the coming third line's output. Order backlog rose 14% to a record, with structural materials margins widening on firmer plate pricing. Steg reaffirmed the third rail plate line remains on schedule for startup next year.

beats.head: Erretmark Works Recalls 480,000 Veyron Vehicles as Braking Probe Concludes
beats.body: Erretmark issued a global recall of 480,000 Veyron units after regulators confirmed a defect in the braking control module that could delay pressure response. The company set aside $310M for repairs and warned the $2.1B fleet accord may see delivery deferrals; Aurelia Garr called it 'a hard but necessary reset' and pledged a redesigned module within the quarter.

beats.head: Lhaus Industries Wins $4.3B Fleet Storage Contract in Landmark Power Division Deal
beats.body: Cole Brandt secured a multi-year agreement to supply Kellstrom-based storage packs to a national logistics fleet operator, the largest single order in the young Power & Storage division's history. The $4.3B contract locks in output through 2032 and validates the $2.1B Kellstrom acquisition Brandt championed. Shares of the vertically integrated automaker reflected the strategic milestone as the division moved from launch to scale.

beats.head: Gromford Works Reels as Emblem Signature Sourcing Claims Trigger Prestige Backlash
beats.body: An industry exposé alleged that Gromford's Emblem Signature Editions used undisclosed third-party casings while marketing them as fully in-house, undercutting the prestige positioning Pryce had chased. CEO Halvard Pryce issued a defensive statement promising a full sourcing audit, but two major stockists paused Signature orders and the Grand Horology Salon opened an inquiry. The controversy lands just as Gromford's margin story hinged on the premium halo.

beats.head: Bruncrest Works Unveils Aria Ultra X, Doubling Throughput Per Line
beats.body: Bruncrest Works revealed the Aria Ultra X, a redesigned compute unit that CEO Ines Marlow said delivers roughly twice the throughput of the current generation while cutting power draw by a third. Marlow claimed the breakthrough lets a single production line match the output of two, easing the margin pressure that dogged last quarter's third-line push. Early commitments from three data-center customers already exceed $3 billion, the company said.
